Trece temas, y cada uno ha dejado una pi: Thirteen topics, and each has left a piece: the [[son-onda|sine]], the [[son-envolvente|envelope]], the [[son-armonicos|harmonics]], the [[son-modulacion|modulation]], the [[son-filtros|filter]], the [[son-ruido|noise]], the [[son-eco|echo]] and the [[son-secuencia|sequencer]]. This topic teaches nothing new: it joins them all into an instrument with every control in view, and leaves you the code to make it your own. Then it says where to go next.
Casi todos los sintetizadores, de 1970 o: Almost all synthesisers, from 1970 or from today, have the same architecture, and you already know all of it. Each box is a topic of this block, and the signal goes from left to right:
la onda cruda: seno, sierra, cuadrada, r: the raw wave: sine, sawtooth, square, noise
quitar agudos, y moverlo con el tiempo: removing high frequencies, and moving it with time
el ataque y la cola de cada nota: the attack and the tail of each note
En el sintetizador de abajo cada etapa e: In the synthesiser below each stage is an auxiliary function, and sonido chains them. The controls touch the most important parameters; everything else is changed in the code. It is long for what a synthesiser of this block usually is, but you have seen every line already.
Una secuencia de ocho notas, cada una co: A sequence of eight notes, each with an oscillator (a mixture of sawtooth and square), vibrato, a filter with its own envelope, a volume envelope and an echo. Play it as it is first. Then change one thing at a time: the list of notes, the waveform, the vibrato speed, the echo delay. When something pleases you, it stays saved in this browser.
Con la resonancia del filtro a cero y el: With the filter resonance at zero and the echo at zero, what is left? A sawtooth with an envelope, playing the list. Turn everything up afterwards and compare.
El eco está a 0,375 s, tres corcheas: ca: The echo is at 0.375 s, three quavers: it always falls off the beat, and that is why it “fills in”. Try 0.25 (a crotchet) or 0.5, and you will see that the same loop sounds like something else. And the vibrato is in semitones, not in hertz, because the ear is logarithmic: that way it moves the same in the low register as in the high.
Cada uno es un cambio pequeño en el códi: Each is a small change in the code above, and in each there is an idea from the block used again. There is no automatic marking: the marker is you, listening.
<strong>Una segunda voz.</strong> Añade: A second voice. Add a bass in crotchets, an octave below the first note of each pair: nota(notas[(2 * floor(n / 2)) % 8] - 12). Add it with its own envelope, and lower the volumes so as not to clip.
<strong>Karplus-Strong en vez del oscila: Karplus-Strong instead of the oscillator. Replace oscilador with the string of [[son-ruido]]: you need the sample index i and to know at which sample the note began ($n \cdot T_p \cdot f_s$).
<strong>Un acorde.</strong> En vez de un: A chord. Instead of one note, three: the one from the list, a major third above (+4 semitones) and a fifth (+7). Check with [[son-batidos]] why +4 and +7 and not +5 and +6.
<strong>Un compás distinto.</strong> Doc: A different time signature. Twelve notes instead of eight, with $T_p$ adjusted so that they fit in the two seconds: that is a bar of 6/8. Or seven, for an irregular bar.
<strong>Una campana FM.</strong> Cambia: An FM bell. Change the oscillator for that of [[son-modulacion]] with ratio 1.41 and a decaying index, and remove the filter: bells come pre-filtered from the factory.
Lo que has usado del curso: What you have used from the course
Merece la pena mirarlo escrito, porque e: It is worth looking at it written down, because it is the answer to the “and what is this for?” heard in every mathematics class: for a loudspeaker to sound.
el seno que suena, la sierra, el periodo: the sine that sounds, the sawtooth, the period and the frequency
la escala de notas ($2^{n/12}$), los cen: the scale of notes ($2^{n/12}$), the cents, the decaying envelope, the decibels
batidos, consonancia, modulación de ampl: beats, consonance, amplitude modulation and its sidebands
el timbre como suma de armónicos; el esp: timbre as a sum of harmonics; the spectrum as a question put to the signal
filtros, Karplus-Strong, el eco y su con: filters, Karplus-Strong, the echo and its convergence
la frecuencia instantánea como derivada: instantaneous frequency as the derivative of the phase; the glissando
el ruido: una variable uniforme por mues: noise: a uniform variable per sample, with its variance
el secuenciador: parte entera y resto: the sequencer: whole part and remainder
de dónde salen los armónicos de una cuer: where the harmonics of a string and of a tube come from
El sintetizador de este bloque es una fu: This block's synthesiser is a function of $t$ computed in full before it sounds. Real ones compute sample by sample while they sound, to react to a keyboard or a control in real time, and that calls for another programming model. These are the doors:
<strong>Web Audio</strong>, en el propio: Web Audio, in the browser itself. The API this block uses only for playback has oscillators, filters, delays and envelopes as nodes that connect to one another, and with an AudioWorklet you write the function sample by sample in JavaScript, as here. Nothing has to be installed.
<strong>Sonic Pi</strong> (sonic-pi.net): Sonic Pi (sonic-pi.net), free, meant for teaching: you write play 60 and it sounds, with ready-made synthesisers and effects and loops that are changed live. Everything from [[son-secuencia]] is there as a language.
<strong>SuperCollider</strong>, el están: SuperCollider, the standard of computer music since 1996: a synthesis server and a language to control it. It is where this block's ideas live on a professional scale, and it is free.
<strong>Pure Data</strong> o <strong>Max: Pure Data or Max: the same, but drawing boxes and cables instead of writing. The chain in the table above, literally connected with the mouse.
<strong>Faust</strong>, un lenguaje dond: Faust, a language where a filter is written as a difference equation and compiles to anything, and the book The Audio Programming Book or Julius Smith's online course Physical Audio Signal Processing, for the whole theory of which this block is the first page.
La música por ordenador nació en 1957 en: Computer music was born in 1957 at Bell Labs, when Max Mathews wrote MUSIC I: a program that computed samples and wrote them onto a tape that was afterwards turned into sound, because the computer was a thousand times too slow to do it live. Exactly this block's model: compute everything, and then listen. His MUSIC V version of 1968 introduced the unit generators, oscillator, envelope, filter, that connect in a chain, the architecture of the table above and of everything that came afterwards, from Csound to SuperCollider. Mathews used to say that the computer was the ultimate instrument: any sound that could be described, it could produce. The description is a function of time, and that is the whole block.
Lo que hace un sintetizador es lo que ha: What a synthesiser does is what any program producing a signal does: a video generator, a circuit simulator, a climate model or a video game's physics engine compute “the next value from the previous ones and from the time”, thousands of times a second. Whoever has written a one-pole filter has written a numerical integrator; whoever has tuned a sequence has handled a real-time clock. And the spectral analysis that here looks at a note looks, elsewhere, at earthquakes, heartbeats, orbits and prices.
El sintetizador de este bloque calcula l: This block's synthesiser computes the whole two seconds before it sounds. What can it therefore not do that a real synthesiser does?
Reaccionar mientras suena: a una tecla,: React while it sounds: to a key, to a control, to a microphone
Todo está decidido antes de la primera m: Everything is decided before the first sample. A real instrument computes each sample at the moment and can change course; for that you need to compute in real time, sample by sample, with the Web Audio or SuperCollider model.
Los usa: <code>anterior</code> y <code>a: It does use them: anterior and antes read what has already been computed. What it cannot do is respond to something happening after the computing.
Suena tan afinado como la fórmula: el cá: It sounds as in tune as the formula: the calculation is the same as that of any digital synthesiser.
Si tocas cinco líneas y suena mal, no sa: If you touch five lines and it sounds bad, you do not know which one it was. One at a time, play, decide.
Cada voz nueva suma amplitud. El aviso d: Each new voice adds amplitude. The synthesiser's clipping warning is there for that: when it appears, lower the volumes.
Poner el filtro después del eco: Putting the filter after the echo
El orden de la cadena importa: filtrar e: The order of the chain matters: filtering the echo dulls the repetitions too; putting the echo after the filter leaves them bright. Try both.
Creer que esto es «lo fácil» y lo de ver: Believing this is “the easy bit” and the real thing is something else
Es lo mismo. Un sintetizador profesional: It is the same. A professional synthesiser is this code, sample by sample, with more stages and in real time. The mathematics does not change.
Cuando quieras saber si el bloque entero: When you want to know whether the whole block has stuck, in [[son-examen]] there is a procedural exam with questions from all its topics, with a clock and marked on submission.
La cadena de un sintetizador: oscilador: The chain of a synthesiser: oscillator → modulation → filter → envelope → effects, and a sequencer that decides which note and when. Each stage is a function.
Todo el bloque cabe en un instrumento de: The whole block fits in a forty-line instrument, and each line is a topic: sines, logarithms, Fourier, recurrences, series, probability, divisibility.
Se cambia una cosa cada vez y se escucha: You change one thing at a time and listen: the marker is the ear.
Para seguir: Web Audio (en el navegador): To go on: Web Audio (in the browser), Sonic Pi (to begin), SuperCollider and Pure Data (for everything), and real-time synthesis, sample by sample.
Cualquier sonido que se pueda describir: Any sound that can be described as a function of time can be produced. That is Max Mathews's idea from 1957, and this block's.
